components.note: 气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.fact: 气 is an important concept: air (空气), weather (天气), breath, energy (the Daoist qi) and anger (生气). 别客气 ('you're welcome', 'don't be so polite') is a very common phrase.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì zhēn hǎo.
examples.english: The weather is really nice today.

examples.pinyin: Bié shēngqì le, wǒ cuò le.
examples.english: Don't be angry, I was wrong.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 不用担心,一切都会好的。
example.pinyin: Bú yòng dānxīn, yíqiè dōu huì hǎo de.
example.english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
example.fact: 不用 politely waves something off as unnecessary ("no need to...") — softer than the flat negative command 不要 ("don’t...") — so being offered tea and answering 不用,谢谢 ("no need, thanks") comes across far gentler than a blunt 不要.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng dānxīn wǒ.
examples.english: You don't need to worry about me.

examples.hanzi: 不用谢,这是我应该做的。
examples.pinyin: Bú yòng xiè, zhè shì wǒ yīnggāi zuò de.
examples.english: No need to thank me, it's what I should do.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
子 (child) — children and offspring, as in 孙 grandchild, 学 study, 字 character; 孩 is a young child.
亥 (hài) is a close sound clue for hái; 亥 also sounds out 该 gāi, 核 hé and 刻 kè.

example.pinyin: Nàge xiǎohái zài gōngyuán lǐ wán.
example.english: That child is playing in the park.
example.fact: 小孩 is the everyday, spoken-register word for "child" — its close relative 孩子 is more neutral and comfortable in both speech and writing, while 小孩(儿) leans distinctly casual and conversational.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoháizi dōu ài chī táng.
examples.english: Kids all love candy.

examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎohái jīnnián sān suì.
examples.english: This child is three this year.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
米 (rice, grain) — the top. Memory aid: grains of rice sorted by size 大 — sorted into groups, a kind (人类). Not proven etymology.
類 (traditional) — used for 'kind, class' with 犬 and 页. 类 is the simplified shape and keeps only a fragment of it.

example.hanzi: 人类是唯一会使用复杂语言的动物。
example.pinyin: Rénlèi shì wéiyī huì shǐyòng fùzá yǔyán de dòngwù.
example.english: Humans are the only animals that use complex language.
example.fact: 类 means "category, kind," so 人类 is literally "the human category" — a species-level term reserved for humanity as a whole, distinct from 人们 ("people," a plural group of individuals) or a single 人 ("a person").

examples.pinyin: Rénlèi xūyào bǎohù huánjìng.
examples.english: Humankind needs to protect the environment.

examples.pinyin: Rénlèi yǐjīng shàngguo yuèqiú.
examples.english: Humans have already been to the moon.

components.note: 冫 (water, ice) — 冲 is the simplified 沖: a water element (冫) beside 中, so water rushing; this form is a water cousin of 冰 and 冷.
中 (zhōng) — near sound — 冲 is chōng; 中 also sounds out 钟 zhōng.

example.fact: 冲 has the readings chōng ('to rush, to flush, to rinse', as in 冲茶, 冲凉) and chòng ('towards, facing', as in 冲着). 冲 is used for brewing tea or coffee with hot water: 冲咖啡.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù chōng yì bēi kāfēi ba.
examples.english: Go make a cup of coffee.

examples.pinyin: Tā chōngchū mén qù zhuī gōngjiāochē.
examples.english: He rushed out the door to catch the bus.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
由 (from, reason) — mostly useful as a sound part: 油 yóu, 邮 yóu, 柚 yòu, 抽 chōu all contain it.

example.hanzi: 每个人都应该享有自由。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi xiǎngyǒu zìyóu.
example.english: Everyone should be entitled to freedom.
example.fact: 由 on its own already carries the sense "from, cause" (as in 由于, "due to") — 自由 combines it with 自 ("self") into "arising from oneself," a literal image of self-determination that happens to parallel the Greek roots of English "autonomy" (autos "self" + nomos "law").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zìyóu de shēnghuó.
examples.english: I like a free life.

examples.hanzi: 周末我可以自由安排时间。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ kěyǐ zìyóu ānpái shíjiān.
examples.english: I can arrange my time freely on weekends.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand holding a branch 十: to prop up, support; 支 also sounds out 枝 zhī branch and 肢 zhī limb.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.

example.english: Thank you all for always supporting me.
example.fact: 支 (a hand holding a branch, "to prop up") and 持 (a hand holding something steady, "to maintain") both independently involve a hand keeping something upright — 支持 combines two "steadying hand" images into the abstract modern sense of supporting a person, cause, or opinion.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhīchí nǐ de juédìng.
examples.english: I support your decision.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xūyào jiārén de zhīchí.
examples.english: He really needs his family's support.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.

example.fact: 星期 names the seven-day week itself (这个星期, "this week") but, attached to a number, also names a single day within it (星期一, literally "week-one," i.e. Monday) — one word doing double duty as both the container and its individual slices, unlike English’s separate "week" and "Monday."

examples.pinyin: Xià ge xīngqī nǐ yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: Are you free next week?

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xīngqī jǐ?
examples.english: What day of the week is it today?

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking, as in 行, 往, 得.
艮 (gèn) is a close sound clue for hěn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 根 gēn, 恨 hèn and 银 yín.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.

example.pinyin: Tā hěn kuài jiù huílái le.
example.fact: 很快 can describe the manner of an action (跑得很快, "runs very fast") or, placed at the front of a clause, shift to mean "soon" about a near-future event (很快就要下雨了, "it’s going to rain very soon") — the same two characters covering both a speed and a near-future timeframe.

examples.pinyin: Hěn kuài, chūntiān jiù lái le.
examples.english: Soon spring arrived.

examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài, yíngle bǐsài.
examples.english: He ran fast and won the race.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 腿 leg, 脸 face.
却 (què) is only a loose sound clue for jiǎo.

example.fact: 脚 is the foot, as opposed to 腿 (leg): 脚趾 (toe), 脚步 (footstep) and 脚印 (footprint). The measure word is 只 for one foot and 双 for a pair.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiǎo bèi xīn xié nòngténg le.
examples.english: My feet are sore from my new shoes.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiǎoxīn, bié cǎidào wǒ de jiǎo.
examples.english: Please be careful not to step on my foot.

components.note: 殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand striking with a tool, as in 殴, 段; 毁 is to wreck.

example.fact: 毁 is a formal verb for destroying: 毁坏 (damage), 毁灭 (destroy), 毁容 (disfigure) and 毁约 (break a contract). It's used for things that can't easily be repaired, unlike 弄坏.

examples.pinyin: Dàshuǐ huǐle hěn duō fángzi.
examples.english: The flood destroyed many houses.

examples.hanzi: 别让一次错误毁了你的计划。
examples.pinyin: Bié ràng yí cì cuòwù huǐle nǐ de jìhuà.
examples.english: Don't let one mistake ruin your plan.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 别生气了,这不是什么大事。
example.pinyin: Bié shēngqì le, zhè bú shì shénme dà shì.
example.english: Don't be angry, this isn't a big deal.
example.fact: 生 ("to arise, to be born") plus 气 ("qi, vital energy") combine into "energy arising" — the same 气 that names the vital life-force in traditional medicine and tai chi, here channeled specifically into the rising heat of anger.

examples.pinyin: Tā shēngqì de zǒule chūqù.
examples.english: He walked out angrily.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bu shì shēngqì le?
examples.english: Are you angry?

components.note: 廴 (long stride) — a rare radical of walking and extending, also in 延 yán and 廷 tíng; 建 means to set up or put up; the sound clue 聿 is only loose.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.

example.fact: 建议 works as both a verb (“to suggest”) and a noun (“a suggestion”) with no change in form — 提出建议 (“to put forward a suggestion”) and 我建议 (“I suggest”) both use the same two characters, one of many Chinese words that cross the verb/noun line freely.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì wǒ duō yùndòng.
examples.english: The doctor advised me to exercise more.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge hěn hǎo de jiànyì.
examples.english: This is a very good suggestion.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 作. 做 is a later variant of 作 zuò (to do), sharing its meaning and sound.
故 (gù) is only a loose sound hint.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我一定会做到我的承诺。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yídìng huì zuòdào wǒ de chéngnuò.
example.english: I will definitely fulfill my promise.
example.fact: 做到 is a verb plus a result complement: 做 (“to do”) plus 到 (“to arrive, reach”) — 到 here doesn't mean physical arrival but marks that the action of 做 actually succeeded, the same “verb + 到 = success” pattern behind 看到 (“to see, to succeed in seeing”) and 听到 (“to hear, to succeed in hearing”).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng zuòdào ma?
examples.english: Can you do it?

examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǔlì, nǐ jiù néng zuòdào.
examples.english: If you work hard, you can achieve it.

components.note: 大 (big/man) — the top part, as in 夫. Dictionary story: a big man wrapped in a long cloth, hence 'cover, set'; used in 外套 coat and 手套 glove.
镸 (long) — the bottom part, a long-hair variant of 長. Memory aid: a long cloth over a big person is a coat or cover.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎile yí tào xīn yīfu.
example.english: I bought a new set of clothes.
example.fact: 套 is a measure word for sets (一套房子, 一套工具), and a verb for putting a cover on: 套上 (put on), 手套 (gloves) and 外套 (coat). It also forms 套路 (routine, or a formula) and 客套 (polite formalities).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí tào xīn jiājù.
examples.english: I want to buy a set of new furniture.

examples.hanzi: 他在外面套了一件外衣。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wàimiàn tàole yí jiàn wàiyī.
examples.english: He pulled a coat on over his clothes.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哭 has two mouths 吅 wailing aloud; 口 marks mouth and voice words, as in 叫 shout, 唱 sing.

example.pinyin: Bié kū le, méi shì le.
example.fact: 哭 is to cry audibly, whereas 流泪 is 'to shed tears' and 眼泪 is the tears. Phrases like 哭笑不得 ('not know whether to laugh or cry') are common.

examples.pinyin: Háizi kūzhe zhǎo māma.
examples.english: The child is crying for his mom.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng ràng wǒ kū le.
examples.english: This movie made me cry.

components.note: 尸 (body, rump) — body-related words: 尿 urine, 屎 dung, 尾 tail, 屋 room; here the buttocks and what comes out.
比 (bǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pì.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 腿 leg, 脚 foot, 肚 belly; 股 is the thigh or rump, later a share.
殳 (shū, weapon in hand) — only a loose sound hint; it also appears in 投 and 设.

example.hanzi: 小孩子摔了一下,屁股很疼。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi shuāi le yíxià, pìgu hěn téng.
example.english: The little kid fell, and their bottom really hurts.
example.fact: 屁股 sits at a casual, everyday register — fine in ordinary conversation the way English “butt” is, but not the word a doctor or formal document would reach for, which would use a more clinical term instead.

examples.hanzi: 他坐在椅子上,屁股很疼。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zài yǐzi shàng, pìgu hěn téng.
examples.english: He sat on the chair and his bottom hurt.

examples.pinyin: Bǎobao de pìgu hónghóng de.
examples.english: The baby's bottom is red.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.

example.fact: 生日 is the plain, everyday word for “birthday” (生 “to be born” + 日 “day”) — for a revered figure's birthday, especially a historical or religious one (as in 孔子诞辰, “Confucius's birthday”), Chinese instead reaches for the more formal and reverent 诞辰, a register distinction with no single English equivalent.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì wǒ de shēngrì.
examples.english: Today is my birthday.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào?
examples.english: What's the date of your birthday?

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.fact: 晚安 works only as a parting word said right before sleep — for an evening greeting said upon arrival, Chinese uses 晚上好 instead, splitting a job that English “good evening” and “good night” also split, but along a slightly different line.

examples.pinyin: Wǎn'ān, míngtiān jiàn.
examples.english: Good night, see you tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 她给妈妈发了一条晚安短信。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi māma fāle yì tiáo wǎn'ān duǎnxìn.
examples.english: She sent her mom a good-night text.

components.note: 不 (bù) is a loose sound clue for fǒu and gives the meaning "not".
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: saying no.
刂 (knife) — cutting and sharp edges: 利 sharp, 刻 carve, 别 divide; 则 meant rules engraved to last. 贝 here is simplified from old 鼎.

example.hanzi: 你要快点,否则就迟到了。
example.pinyin: Nǐ yào kuàidiǎn, fǒuzé jiù chídào le.
example.english: You need to hurry, otherwise you'll be late.
example.fact: 否则 almost always sets up a clause that follows with 就 (“否则就...”), the same way 如果 pairs with 就 — 就 marks the natural, almost automatic consequence of whatever comes before it.

examples.hanzi: 快点走,否则赶不上火车了。
examples.pinyin: Kuài diǎn zǒu, fǒuzé gǎn bu shàng huǒchē le.
examples.english: Hurry up, or we won't catch the train.

examples.hanzi: 你必须按时吃药,否则病不会好。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bìxū ànshí chī yào, fǒuzé bìng bú huì hǎo.
examples.english: You must take your medicine on time, otherwise you won't get better.

components.note: 田 (field) — 画 (simplified 畫) originally showed a brush 聿 drawing the borders of a field: to draw lines, hence a picture.

example.pinyin: Tā zài huà yì zhī māo.
example.fact: 画 is both verb and noun: 画画儿 (draw), 一幅画 (a painting), 画家 (painter). 画 is also the stroke of a character in 笔画 (strokes), so 'how many strokes' is 几画.

examples.pinyin: Tā huàle yì fú piàoliang de huà.
examples.english: She drew a beautiful picture.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò qù xué huàhuà.
examples.english: I go to learn painting on weekends.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.

example.fact: 病 is illness: 生病 (to get sick), 看病 (see a doctor), 病人 (patient) and 病毒 (virus). 病 can also be a fault: 语病 means 'a grammar error'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma bìng le, zài yīyuàn.
examples.english: My mom is sick and in the hospital.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō nǐ de bìng bù yánzhòng.
examples.english: The doctor says your illness isn't serious.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.

example.fact: 线 is thread, line or wire, and also route: 线路 (circuit, route), 电线 (cable), 在线 (online) and 路线 (route). 在线 is the standard word for 'online'.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gēn xiàn tài xì le, bù jiēshi.
examples.english: This thread is too thin and not strong.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zài xiànshàng yùdìng fángjiān.
examples.english: Please book a room online.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire above a person (儿 legs) — a person carrying fire gives light; 光 is bright and shining, as in 阳光, 时光.
儿 (legs, person) — the bottom 儿 is a walking person, seen also in 先, 兄, 元.

example.fact: 光 is light, as in 阳光 (sunshine), 月光 and 光明. It also means 'only' or 'used up': 光吃饭 (just eating), 吃光 (eat it all up). 光 can describe a smooth surface too: 光滑.

examples.pinyin: Chuāngwài de yángguāng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The sunlight outside the window is lovely.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang de qián dōu huāguāng le.
examples.english: All the money on the table has been spent.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.

example.pinyin: Zhècì lǚxíng shì shéi ānpái de?
example.fact: 安排 crosses freely between verb (“to arrange”) and noun (“an arrangement, a plan”) — 工作安排 (“work arrangements”) needs no different word than 我安排了这次旅行 (“I arranged this trip”).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái ānpái míngtiān de huìyì.
examples.english: I'll arrange tomorrow's meeting.

examples.hanzi: 今天的工作已经安排好了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de gōngzuò yǐjīng ānpái hǎo le.
examples.english: Today's work has already been planned.

components.note: 年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport, 较 compare; 轻 was a light cart.
The right half is a short form of 巠 (jīng), the sound part in 经 jīng, 径 jìng and 茎 jīng — a loose clue for qīng.

example.fact: 轻 on its own means “light” in weight, as its own etymology (a light, nimble cart) shows — 年轻 borrows that sense of lightness metaphorically for a person's age, pairing 年 (“years”) with an image of being unburdened by age, not unlike English describing someone as having a “youthful lightness.”

examples.pinyin: Tā bǐ wǒ niánqīng wǔ suì.
examples.english: She's five years younger than me.

examples.pinyin: Niánqīngrén yīnggāi duō xuéxí.
examples.english: Young people should study more.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.

example.fact: 神 is god, spirit and mind: 神仙 (immortal), 神话 (myth), 精神 (spirit, vigour) and 神秘 (mysterious). As an adjective in slang, 神 means amazing: 神奇.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān kàn qǐlái méi jīngshen.
examples.english: You look listless today.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hěn shénqí de rén.
examples.english: He is a very amazing person.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 操 is to handle or drill.
喿 (zào) hints at the sound: 操 cāo is close to 澡 zǎo and 燥 zào.

example.fact: 操 means to grasp, drill or exercise: 体操 (gymnastics), 早操 (morning exercises), 操作 (operate) and 操心 (to worry about). The very rude word 操 is a vulgar slang, so avoid it in everyday talk.

examples.pinyin: Māma zǒngshì wèi háizi cāoxīn.
examples.english: Mom always worries about her children.

examples.hanzi: 同学们在操场上做早操。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxuémen zài cāochǎng shang zuò zǎocāo.
examples.english: The students are doing morning exercises on the field.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.english: Please look at the example below.
example.fact: Beyond its literal spatial sense “below,” 下面 is a common discourse marker for “next” in speech and writing (下面我们介绍..., “next, we will introduce...”) — a physical direction word repurposed as a tool for organizing what comes next in a talk or text.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā jiù zài yínháng xiàmian.
examples.english: My home is right below the bank.

examples.pinyin: Xiàmian qǐng tīng xià yì shǒu gē.
examples.english: Next, please listen to the next song.

components.note: 女 (woman) — female kin and women: 妈 mom, 姐 sister, 妹 younger sister, 娘; 姑 is a father's sister.
古 (gǔ) is close to gū; the series includes 估 gū, 枯 kū, 苦 kǔ and 故 gù.
女 (woman) — mothers and girls: 妈, 姑, 姐; 娘 is mother or young woman, as in 新娘 bride.
良 (liáng) is a loose sound hint (-iang); same part in 狼 láng and 浪 làng.

example.hanzi: 那个姑娘唱歌唱得真好。
example.pinyin: Nàge gūniang chàng gē chàng de zhēn hǎo.
example.fact: 姑娘 carries a warmer, slightly old-fashioned or rural flavor next to the plainer, more modern 女孩 — a register difference worth noticing before picking between the two, not unlike English “lass” sitting beside plain “girl.”

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gūniang shì wǒ de línjū.
examples.english: This young woman is my neighbor.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gūniang, nǐ zài zhǎo shénme?
examples.english: Little girl, what are you looking for?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.fact: 道 is a road and a way, and the root of 道理 (reason), 知道 (know), 道歉 (apologise) and 道德 (morals). It is also the Dao (道) of Daoism. In classical or opera speech it means 'to say'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào tā zhù nǎr ma?
examples.english: Do you know where he lives?

examples.hanzi: 请问，这条街的人行道在哪里？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, zhè tiáo jiē de rénxíngdào zài nǎlǐ?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the sidewalk on this street?

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 按 is to press with the hand, as in 按摩 massage.
安 (ān) — same sound, different tone — 按 is àn; 安 also sounds out 案 àn.

example.fact: 按 is to press, and as a preposition it means 'according to': 按时 (on time), 按照 (in accordance with), 按钮 (button). 按摩 is massage.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ àn yíxià zhège jiàn.
examples.english: Press this key.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng ànshí chī yào.
examples.english: Please take your medicine on time.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals and metal tools: 钱 money, 铁 iron, 针 needle; a key is made of metal.
月 (yuè) is close to yuè/yào.
匕 (spoon) — a rare radical meaning ladle or spoon; here 匙 chí is a spoon and in 钥匙 it is read neutral shi.
是 (shì) is a rough sound clue for chí/shi.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yàoshi wàng zài jiā lǐ le.
example.english: I forgot my keys at home.
example.fact: 钥匙 pairs 钥 (a metal-radical character tied to locks) with 匙, the same character that independently means “spoon” (as in 汤匙, “soup spoon”) — a widely repeated, if hard to fully verify, explanation traces this to older keys having a long, thin, spoon-like shape.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàndào wǒ de yàoshi le ma?
examples.english: Have you seen my keys?

examples.pinyin: Yàoshi zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.english: The keys are on the table.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 法官宣布了最终的判决。
example.pinyin: Fǎguān xuānbù le zuìzhōng de pànjué.
example.english: The judge announced the final verdict.
example.fact: 法官 literally combines 法 (“law”) with 官 (“official”) — “law official” — the same building pattern behind other government-role words like 警官 (“police officer”) and 长官 (“commanding officer”).

examples.pinyin: Fǎguān tīngle shuāngfāng de yìjiàn.
examples.english: The judge listened to both sides.

examples.hanzi: 他想长大后成为一名法官。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zhǎngdà hòu chéngwéi yì míng fǎguān.
examples.english: He wants to become a judge when he grows up.

components.note: 勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.

example.fact: 包 means to wrap (包饺子), and as a noun it's a bag or package: 书包, 钱包 (wallet), 面包 (bread) and 包子 (steamed bun). It's also a measure word for packs: 一包烟.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shūbāo lǐ yǒu yì běn shū.
examples.english: There is a book in my school bag.

examples.pinyin: Nǎinai bāo de jiǎozi zuì hǎochī.
examples.english: The dumplings Grandma makes are the best.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脚 foot, 脸 face.
退 (tuì) gives the same syllable with a different tone.

example.fact: 腿 is the leg, from thigh to foot: 大腿 (thigh), 小腿 (calf), 腿疼 (leg ache). Food terms use it too: 鸡腿 (chicken drumstick) and 火腿 (ham).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tuǐ pǎobù pǎo de hěn lèi.
examples.english: My legs are tired from running.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi yǒu sì tiáo tuǐ.
examples.english: This table has four legs.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).

example.fact: 自 is a bound form meaning 'self': 自己 (oneself), 自由 (freedom), 自然 (nature), 自信 (self-confidence), and 'from' in 来自 (come from). Its shape is the nose, and a person pointing at their nose means themselves.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zìjǐ néng zuò ma?
examples.english: Can you do it by yourself?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zìcóng bānlái jiù hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: I've been happy ever since I moved here.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 每个国家都派出了自己的选手。
example.pinyin: Měi gè guójiā dōu pàichū le zìjǐ de xuǎnshǒu.
example.english: Every country sent its own athletes.
example.fact: 选手 literally “selected hand” (选 “to select” + 手, here meaning “a person skilled at something,” as in 高手 “expert”) — the word specifically implies someone chosen through competition, not just any participant or player.

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi xuǎnshǒu pǎo de hěn kuài.
examples.english: This athlete runs very fast.

examples.hanzi: 比赛前,选手们都很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài qián, xuǎnshǒumen dōu hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: Before the match, the contestants were all nervous.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
自 (nose) — over 心 heart: breath comes through the nose from the heart, so rest, news.

example.pinyin: Qǐng tígōng gèng duō de xìnxī.
example.fact: 信息 already meant “news, information” well before the computer age, but it's now closely tied to computing-era terms like 信息技术 (“information technology”) — pairing 信 (“letter, trust”) with 息 (“breath, news”), an old vocabulary combination that just happened to fit a 20th-century concept perfectly.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǒujī lǐ yǒu tā de xìnxī.
examples.english: I have his information on my phone.

examples.hanzi: 网上有很多有用的信息。
examples.pinyin: Wǎng shàng yǒu hěn duō yǒuyòng de xìnxī.
examples.english: There's a lot of useful information online.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.

example.pinyin: Wǒ děngle zhěngzhěng yí gè xiǎoshí.
example.fact: 整 means whole and also neat: 整个 (the whole), 整齐 (tidy), 整理 (to sort out) and 整天 (all day). In dialect, 整 also means 'to do' or 'to mess with': 整人 (play a trick on someone).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhěnggè zhōumò dōu zài jiā.
examples.english: I'm at home all weekend long.

examples.hanzi: 他把房间整理得很干净。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ fángjiān zhěnglǐ de hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: He tidied the room until it was clean.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 投 is to throw.
殳 (shū) is a weapon-in-hand part that is only a loose sound clue; it also appears in 设 shè and 段 duàn.
票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.hanzi: 我们下周要投票选新班长。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xià zhōu yào tóupiào xuǎn xīn bānzhǎng.
example.english: We're going to vote for a new class monitor next week.
example.fact: 投票 literally means “to throw a ticket” (投 “to throw, cast” + 票 “ticket, note”) — the same 投 that shows up in 投篮 (“to shoot a basketball”) and 投递 (“to deliver mail”), all sharing the sense of propelling something toward a target.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān qù tóupiào le ma?
examples.english: Did you go vote today?

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā jǔshǒu tóupiào ba.
examples.english: Everyone, raise your hands to vote.

components.note: 可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).
可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).

example.pinyin: Wǒ gēge bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
example.english: My older brother is three years older than me.
example.fact: Chinese kinship terms mark birth order where English just says “brother” — 哥哥 is strictly an older brother, and a younger one is 弟弟, a distinction with no single-word English equivalent.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge zài Shànghǎi gōngzuò.
examples.english: My older brother works in Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Gēge, nǐ néng bāng wǒ yíxià ma?
examples.english: Brother, can you help me?

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.

example.fact: The verb that pairs with 手术 is the generic 做 (“to do”) — 做手术 (“to do/perform/undergo surgery”) covers both the surgeon performing the operation and the patient undergoing it, with context alone telling the two roles apart.

examples.pinyin: Shǒushù hěn chénggōng.
examples.english: The surgery was very successful.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā xūyào zuò shǒushù.
examples.english: The doctor said he needs surgery.

components.note: 必 (bì) is a sound clue for 秘 mì, 密 mì and 蜜 mì: the same series, with only the initial changing.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.english: There's no need to worry so much.
example.fact: 必要 (“necessary, a necessity,” used with 有/没有) is often confused with the similar-sounding 必须 (“must,” an adverb placed directly before a verb) — 有必要 (“it is necessary”) and 必须做 (“must do”) reveal the underlying grammatical split between the two.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu bìyào zhèyàng zuò ma?
examples.english: Is it necessary for you to do this?

examples.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ shì bìyào de.
examples.english: Drinking more water is necessary.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí péi zài wǒ shēnbiān.
example.english: She has always stayed by my side.
example.fact: 身边 is literally “body-side” (身 “body” + 边 “side, edge”) — attaching a possessive pronoun before it (我身边, 你身边) is the standard Chinese way to say “near me / near you,” where English instead reaches for a preposition like “beside” or “near.”

examples.pinyin: Tā shēnbiān méiyǒu jiārén.
examples.english: He has no family by his side.

examples.hanzi: 我身边总有朋友陪着我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēnbiān zǒng yǒu péngyou péizhe wǒ.
examples.english: I always have friends with me.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.fact: 知 on its own is formal. The everyday verb is 知道, 'to know a fact'. Compounds include 通知 (notice), 知识 (knowledge) and 无知 (ignorant). It is different from 认识, which means to know a person.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā zài nǎr.
examples.english: I don't know where he is.

examples.pinyin: Tā de zhīshi hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: He has a wealth of knowledge.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 任何人都可以参加这个比赛。
example.pinyin: Rènhérén dōu kěyǐ cānjiā zhège bǐsài.
example.english: Anyone can participate in this competition.
example.fact: 任何 (“any, whatever”) almost always pairs with 都 right after its noun (任何人都..., “anyone/everyone without exception...”) — 都 here doesn't mean “also” but reinforces totality, the same reinforcing job it does when question words turn into “any-” words, as in 谁都 or 什么都.

examples.hanzi: 这件事任何人都不能说。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì rènhé rén dōu bù néng shuō.
examples.english: Nobody can talk about this.

examples.hanzi: 你在这里看到任何人了吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhèlǐ kàndào rènhé rén le ma?
examples.english: Have you seen anyone here?

components.note: 票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.fact: 票 takes the measure word 张 and covers tickets (车票, 门票), votes (投票) and bills (钞票). It's also used for a 'ticket' in the sense of a pass: 机票 (plane ticket).

examples.pinyin: Huǒchēpiào duōshao qián yì zhāng?
examples.english: How much is a train ticket?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ mǎidào diànyǐngpiào le ma?
examples.english: Did you get movie tickets?

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 撒 is scattering or letting go.
散 (sàn) scatter is the meaning-sound part: a hand 扌 scattering, with sā/sàn close in sound.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说, 话, 请; 谎 is a spoken lie.
荒 (huāng) sounds the same as 谎 huǎng except for tone; also 慌 huāng.

example.fact: 撒谎 is literally “to scatter a lie” (撒 “to scatter, cast” + 谎 “lie, falsehood”) — the same 撒 appears in 撒盐 (“to sprinkle salt”) and 撒网 (“to cast a net”), all built on the image of throwing something loosely outward.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào duì wǒ sāhuǎng.
examples.english: Don't lie to me.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi sāhuǎng shì bú duì de.
examples.english: It's wrong for kids to lie.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot stepping forward with a weapon 戈 (spear-axe): marching armed, hence military; seen in 武器 weapon.
Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.

example.hanzi: 警察在他家发现了武器。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài tā jiā fāxiàn le wǔqì.
example.english: The police found weapons at his home.
example.fact: 武器 is literally “martial tool” (武 “military, martial” + 器 “vessel, tool, instrument”) — the same productive 器 gives 乐器 (“musical instrument”) and 电器 (“electrical appliance”), a recurring suffix for “tool/device of X kind.”

examples.hanzi: 博物馆里有古代的武器。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu gǔdài de wǔqì.
examples.english: There are ancient weapons in the museum.

examples.pinyin: Yóuxì lǐ de wǔqì hěn kù.
examples.english: The weapons in the game are cool.
